description: Batch vectors: request and cancel batches run per item, execute batches are atomic, item counts at 0, MAX_BATCH and MAX_BATCH + 1, and the transfer budget at 18 and 19 transfers.

vectors.description: A request batch of MAX_BATCH items is accepted and records every item in order.
Request batches of 0 and MAX_BATCH + 1 items are BATCH_INVALID and record nothing; one item is accepted.
In a three item request batch the second item is refused: items one and three are recorded, and only the second emits payout_request_rejected.
An ID repeated later in the same request batch is PAYOUT_ID_EXISTS, and the first item's record is kept.
Each request item sees the reservations of the items before it: 600 leaves 400 free, so 500 is refused and 400 fits.
Every refused item reports its own first failing check and the batch carries on with the next item.
The caller, pause and length checks refuse the whole request batch before any item runs, so no item emits anything.
A cancel batch of MAX_BATCH items cancels each one in order with reason 1 and releases every reservation.
Cancel batches of 0 and MAX_BATCH + 1 IDs are BATCH_INVALID and cancel nothing; one ID is accepted.
Cancel batch items fail one by one: an unknown ID, an executed payout and a repeat are refused while the others are cancelled.
Who may cancel is decided per item: a third party cancels only the lapsed payout, and an agent only its own.
After revoke a cancel batch is MANDATE_REVOKED before its length is checked.
An execute batch of MAX_BATCH single-leg payouts without a fee pays every item in order, with spent growing item by item.
Execute batches of 0 and MAX_BATCH + 1 approved IDs are BATCH_INVALID and pay nothing; one ID is accepted.
In a three item execute batch the second item's destination was removed: the call fails with its code, emits nothing and moves no balance.
An execute batch fails with the code of its first failing item, whichever later items would also fail.
Nine two-leg payouts are exactly MAX_BATCH_TRANSFERS transfers and execute in one batch.
Ten two-leg payouts are 20 transfers: the tenth item breaks MAX_BATCH_TRANSFERS, the batch is BATCH_INVALID, and the first nine then execute.
Nine two-leg payouts and one single-leg payout are 19 transfers and BATCH_INVALID; without one two-leg item the rest fit.
A fee is one more transfer: eight two-leg payouts plus a two-leg payout with a fee are 19 and refused, while a single-leg payout with a fee makes exactly 18.
An item that breaks its own rule reports that rule even when it would also break the transfer budget.
The caller, pause and length checks refuse the whole execute batch before any item runs.
After a clawback leaves 700 against 1000 committed, each item's balance check sees what earlier items paid: either order fails at its second item, though each item alone fits.
When the second item's destination cannot receive, the whole execute batch is TRANSFER_FAILED and the first item's payment is reverted too.
